request.spec:
Keep a list of people on the sheet. Each has a name (required; an empty name is refused with an
error on the form) and a grade, one of A, B or C. People are added through a form, and an
existing person can be edited through the same form (opening a person's editor fills the form
with their values). Show all the people in the order they were added, each with their name and
grade.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Keep a list of people on the sheet. Each has a name (required; an empty name is refused with an
error on the form) and a grade, one of A, B or C. People are added through a form, and an
existing person can be edited through the same form (opening a person's editor fills the form
with their values). Show all the people in the order they were added, each with their name and
grade.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added a people list to the sheet, and the test in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` now passes with `bin/e2e`.

**Stored data:** a new migration, `V3__person.sql`, adds a `person` table. Each person is stored against their sheet with a name, a grade and who added them. People are listed in the order they were added.

**Server** (OfficeFloor YAML under `rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/`, Java in `net.officefloor.hq.app.person`):
- `GET .../people` lists the sheet's people.
- `POST .../people` adds a person.
- `PUT .../people/{personId}` edits a person.
- Both the add and the edit check the name and grade first. A name that is empty after trimming, or a grade other than A, B or C, is refused with an error and nothing is saved. An edit of a person that doesn't exist is refused as not found.
- Names are saved with leading and trailing spaces removed, so `" ada "` is stored as `ada`. The test still passes because it ignores outer spaces.

**Front end** (`features/people/`): the people section fills the sheet's existing content area. One form does both adding and editing. A person's Edit button fills the form with their values and shows a Cancel button. An error appears when a save is refused and disappears when you change the form or submit again. Each person's row shows their name and grade.

**Problem found on the way:** the first version saved the person but sent back an empty reply, so the screen showed the add as refused. The cause was in getting the new person's id after the insert: the database hands back more than one generated value (the id and the created time), and asking for "the key" threw an error. I fixed it by asking for the `id` column only. The server also turned that error into an empty `200` and the row was still saved. That's a general weakness in the app's error handling that I didn't change; it could hide other failures the same way.

Nothing is written to the audit file, because the test doesn't expect any audit records.
